title: Cap. 7 Rat. 10: conditional-only merit leaves us no better off in Christ than in Adam
pass_a_gloss: If therefore Christ by his death should not have merited grace and life for any human beings absolutely, but for all promiscuously under this uncertain condition—If they should have been willing to admit the offered grace, to believe in him, and to persevere in Faith—and meanwhile should commit and leave it to each one's free choice whether he wills to believe, wills to persevere or not; then indeed, as regards the very mode and certainty of obtaining efficacious grace and eternal life, we should use a condition no better in Christ than that which we used in Adam.
pass_b_english: So if by his death Christ did not merit grace and life for anyone absolutely, but only for all alike under the uncertain condition that they choose to receive the offered grace, believe in him, and persevere in faith, leaving to each person's free choice whether to believe and persevere, then we would be no better off in Christ than we were in Adam. That is so as to how and how surely we obtain efficacious grace and eternal life.
source_text: Si ergo Christus morte sua non meruerit gratiam vitamque ullis hominibus absolute, sed omnibus promiscue sub hac incerta conditione, Si voluerint oblatam gratiam admittere, in ipsum credere, & in Fide perseverare, atque interim libero uniuscujusque arbitrio committat & relinquat, utrum velit credere, velit perseverare necne; profecto quod attinet ad ipsum modum & certitudinem obtinendae gratiae efficacis & vitae aeternae, nihilo meliore conditione uteremur in Christo, quam usi fuimus in Adamo.
